title: Marine Acquisition Officer-Aviation (I) (MajGen to Maj) PMOS, MCSC
raw_text:
27. MOS 8059, Marine Acquisition Officer-Aviation (I) (MajGen to Maj) PMOS,
MCSC

    a. Summary. A Marine Acquisition Officer-Aviation is selected from a
panel of eligible candidates for lateral transition into the occupation
field. This officer is normally assigned to critical acquisition positions
(CAP) or key leadership positions (KLP), per guidance found in the DoDI 5000
series. They provide senior level leadership over aviation equities



                                           1-326                        Enclosure (1)
 1144                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



throughout the entire acquisition lifecycle. The MOS ensures a sufficient
pool of senior acquisition leaders exist to assume the role of Acquisition
Category I-IV (ACAT I-IV) Program Manager, Fleet Repair Center (FRC)
Commanding Officer, or Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Commanding
Officer for Marine Corps equities.



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess FMOS 8057.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (3) Unrestricted officers holding a primary MOS from OccFld 60XX,
66XX, 72XX, 73XX, or 75XX.

        (4) Must be a major select or higher who has less than 24 years of
active commissioned service as of 1 June of the current fiscal year (FY); and
who is not currently slated for command as a result of the current FY command
screening board.

    c. Requirements.        Assignment will be based on selection by a panel of
eligible candidates.

    d. Duties. The Marine Acquisition Officer-Aviation is key to the entire
systems acquisition process. They are accountable for taking a new validated
requirement from concept exploration to the deployment and sustainment of an
operational piece of equipment to its eventful disposal-cradle to grave. In
broad terms, responsibilities involve keeping a program within budget, on
schedule, meeting key performance parameters, and ensuring life-cycle
sustainability and proper disposal. Specific responsibilities include, but
not limited to, the following tasks program initiation, justification and
validation; cost analysis and estimation; system development program
management; systems engineering management; manpower and training systems
management; life cycle system support management; program financial
management; providing planning, programming and budgeting system support to
acquisition program and appropriate USMC/USN appropriation sponsors; and
program technical data and documentation planning.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Purchasing Managers 11-3061.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     Marine Acquisition Officer-Ground, 8061.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
